purpose: Primary and official sources used to design the Arabic, French, and Urdu graded reading curriculum.

sources.title: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR): descriptors and reading comprehension resources
sources.use: A1-C2 progression, reading purposes, inference, longer/complex text and implicit-meaning targets

sources.title: Unknown vocabulary density and reading comprehension
sources.use: lexical coverage and comprehensibility; supports keeping ordinary fluency reading near the high-90% known-token range

sources.title: The Percentage of Words Known in a Text and Reading Comprehension
sources.use: lexical coverage has an approximately continuous relationship with comprehension; avoid treating 95/98% as magical cutoffs

sources.title: Unknown Vocabulary Density and Reading Comprehension: Replicating Hu and Nation (2000)
sources.use: modern replication and direct testing of multiple lexical-coverage conditions

sources.title: At what rate do learners learn and retain new vocabulary from reading a graded reader?
sources.use: incidental word learning is gradual; repeated encounters improve learning and retention

sources.title: Contextual Word Learning in the First and Second Language: Definition Placement and Inference Error Effects on Declarative and Nondeclarative Knowledge
sources.use: infer-then-verify design for new vocabulary; corrective feedback after contextual inference

sources.title: Contextual Word Learning During Reading in a Second Language
sources.use: word-form familiarity develops faster than fluent semantic integration; motivates repeated contextual encounters

sources.title: The effects of contextual diversity on incidental vocabulary learning
sources.use: begin with narrow/thematically related contexts at low proficiency, then increase genre/topic diversity as lexical knowledge grows

sources.title: Effects of Opportunities for Word Retrieval During Second Language Vocabulary Learning
sources.author: Joe Barcroft
sources.use: retrieval opportunities improve L2 word retention; supports post-reading recall and cloze

sources.title: Mixing Grammar Exercises Facilitates Long-Term Retention: Effects of Blocking, Interleaving, and Increasing Practice
sources.use: interleaving supports delayed L2 grammar retention; begin with supported patterns then mix old and new structures

sources.title: Does spaced practice have the same effects on different second language vocabulary learning activities? Fill-in-the-blanks versus flashcards
sources.use: spaced fill-in-the-blank practice can support delayed vocabulary retention; motivates spaced cloze transfer items

sources.title: The Effect of Pleasure Reading on Japanese University EFL Learners' Reading Rates
sources.use: substantial easy/simplified reading can improve L2 reading rate without sacrificing comprehension

sources.title: Promoting L2 reading fluency at the tertiary level through timed and repeated reading
sources.use: timed/repeated fluency work; study used approximately 350-word passages followed by comprehension questions

sources.title: Arabic L2 readability assessment: Dimensionality reduction study
sources.use: Arabic readability is multidimensional; lexical, morphological and syntactic features matter beyond raw sentence length

sources.title: Predictors of Reading in Urdu: Does Deep Orthography Have an Impact?
sources.use: Urdu orthography/diacritic omission and script complexity require conservative early decoding load and careful fluency interpretation

sources.title: Evaluating Lexical Simplification and Vocabulary Knowledge for Learners of French: Possibilities of Using the FLELex Resource
sources.use: French learner-oriented lexical grading and text complexity checks
